entries.name: Finite-difference least square methods for solving Hamilton-Jacobi equations using neural networks
entries.abstract: We present a simple algorithm to approximate the viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equations by means of an artificial deep neural network. The algorithm uses a stochastic gradient descent-based method to minimize the least square principle defined by a monotone, consistent numerical scheme. We analyze the least square principle's critical points and derive conditions that guarantee that any critical point approximates the sought viscosity solution. The use of a deep artificial neural network on a finite difference scheme lifts the restriction of conventional finite difference methods that rely on computing functions on a fixed grid. This feature makes it possible to solve HJ equations posed in higher dimensions where conventional methods are infeasible. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm through numerical studies on various canonical HJ equations across different dimensions, showcasing its potential and versatility.

entries.name: Almost Sure Convergence Rates and Concentration of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning with Markovian Noise
entries.abstract: This paper establishes, to our knowledge, the first almost sure convergence rate and the first maximal concentration bound with sub-Weibull tails for general contractive stochastic approximation algorithms with Markovian noise. As a corollary, we also obtain convergence rates in $L^p$. Key to our successes is a novel discretization of the mean ODE of stochastic approximation algorithms using intervals with diminishing (instead of constant) length. Applications yield the first almost sure convergence rate for $Q$-learning without count-based learning rates and the first maximal concentration bound for off-policy temporal difference learning, both with Markovian samples.

entries.name: Extensions of Robbins-Siegmund Theorem with Applications in Reinforcement Learning
entries.abstract: The Robbins-Siegmund theorem establishes the convergence of stochastic processes that are almost supermartingales and is one of the most commonly used approaches for analyzing stochastic iterative algorithms in stochastic approximation and reinforcement learning (RL). However, its original form has a significant limitation as it requires the zero-order term to be summable. In many important RL applications, this summable condition, however, cannot be met. This limitation motivates us to extend the Robbins-Siegmund theorem for almost supermartingales where the zero-order term is not summable, but only square-summable. In particular, we introduce a novel and mild assumption on the increments of the stochastic processes. This together with the square-summable condition enables an almost sure convergence to a bounded set. Additionally, we further provide almost sure convergence rates, high probability concentration bounds, and $L^p$ convergence rates. We then apply the new results to stochastic approximation and RL. Notably, we obtain the first almost sure convergence rate, the first high probability concentration bound, and the first $L^p$ convergence rate for $Q$-learning with linear function approximation.

entries.name: A convenient category of locales
entries.abstract: The notion of Kan extendable subcategories was initially introduced to define the category of compactly generated fibrewise topological spaces over a T1 base space and to establish its cartesian closure. In this paper, we show that the same framework can likewise be applied to define the category of compactly generated strongly Hausdorff locales and to prove that it, too, is cartesian closed

entries.name: Adjusting SPRT for an Asymptotically Efficient Procedure with Finite Number of Applications of Less Effective Treatment
entries.abstract: We propose an adaptive Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) with a finite expected number of allocations to the less effective treatment. In the classical SPRT framework, patients are assigned to the two competing treatments one-by-one until a stopping criterion, based on breaching the boundary values which are pre-determined using the Type-I and Type-II error probabilities, is met. This controls the errors at the cost of ethical efficiency as the exposure to the less effective treatment is large. For testing two simple hypotheses, our proposed procedure employs a likelihood ratio-driven adaptive allocation rule, dynamically concentrating sampling effort on the superior population while preserving asymptotic efficiency (in terms of average sample number) comparable to the classical SPRT. We show that at each step, the allocated observations remain independent despite the data-dependent allocation, prove that the expected number of allocations to the inferior treatment remains finite, with an explicit upper bound, and derive a closed-form approximation to it. Extensive simulation studies and data-calibrated case studies substantiate the theoretical results, evincing a significant reduction in inferior allocations compared to the classical SPRT. The proposed design thus offers a balanced method between statistical precision and ethical responsibility, aligning inferential reliability with patient safety.

entries.name: Weighted boundedness for the maximal operator associated with matrices
entries.abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness on $L^p(w)$ of the maximal operator $M_{A^{-1}}$, defined by $M_{A^{-1}}f(x)=Mf(A^{-1}x)$, that is, the maximal of Hardy-Littlewood composed with a invertible matrix $A$. We present two different results of boundedness and provide a characterization for a particular case of matrices. The main novelty lies in examples illustrating the difference between the class of weights with a matrix, $\mathcal{A}_{A,p}$, and the classical Muckenhoupt weight class, $\mathcal{A}_{p}$. Finally, we extend these results to the fractional framework, considering the fractional maximal operator $M_{α, A^{-1}}$.

entries.name: The maximum Cox complexity of a Fano-type variety and the Mukai conjecture
entries.abstract: We define an intrinsic invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(\cdot)$, the maximum Cox complexity, of Fano-type varieties $X$. We prove $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$ and $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)=0$ if and only if $X$ is toric. We then apply this invariant to the Mukai conjecture, which characterises powers of projective spaces among smooth Fano varieties in terms of $\dim(X)$, the Picard number $ρ(X)$, and the Fano index $i(X)$. All klt Fano varieties $X$ canonically embed into a projective toric variety $Z$ via their Cox ring. When $Z$ is smooth, we call $X$ ambiently smooth. We prove the Mukai conjecture for ambiently smooth Fano varieties by establishing the stronger inequality: $\dim(X)+ρ(X)-i(X)ρ(X)\geqγ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\geq 0$. Notably, 45% of the deformation families of smooth Fano threefolds have an ambiently smooth member. For a Fano-type variety $X$, the invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$ is defined using coefficient sums of anticanonical divisors supported on the divisors corresponding to minimal homogeneous generators of the Cox ring. Our proof proceeds by reducing the Cox ring to positive characteristic, using strong F-regularity to obtain the coefficients of an anticanonical divisor, and the F-pure threshold to establish the nonnegativity of $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$.

entries.name: Thresholds for Tic-Tac-Toe on Finite Affine Spaces
entries.abstract: We study the strong positional game in which two players alternately claim points of $\F_q^m$ and the first to complete an affine $n$-subspace wins. We distinguish the first winning dimension $τ(n,q)$ from the eventual winning threshold $T(n,q)$, without assuming monotonicity in $m$. Affine Ramsey theory proves finiteness, while the Erdős-Selfridge criterion and explicit geometric strategies give lower bounds. In the binary case, a quantitative form of the classical quotient argument yields $T(n,2)\le2^{n-1}+n$, with a corresponding bound for any number of colors. A plane-counting recursion gives further multicolor and extremal estimates. We prove $τ(2,2)=T(2,2)=4$ and show that every $31$-point subset of $\F_2^6$ contains an affine $3$-subspace. This gives an elementary proof of the known equality $\AR_2(3;2)=6$ and implies $τ(3,2)=T(3,2)\in\{5,6\}$. Previously known planar outcomes are recovered within the same framework.

entries.name: Geometric Properties of positive solutions of Lane-Emden problems on convex domains of $§^2$
entries.abstract: We study positive solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu = u^p$ in a uniformly convex domain $Ω\subset §^2$, $u= 0$ on $\partialΩ.$ For $p=1$, we assume that the right-hand side is replaced by $λ_1 u$, where $λ_1$ is the first eigenvalue of $-Δ$ on $Ω$ with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that for $0 \leq p < 1$ the unique positive solution $u$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly concave in $Ω$, while for $1 < p \leq 3$ every positive solution $u$ which belongs to the connected component of the least-energy branch of solutions issued from $p=1$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly convex in $Ω$.

entries.name: Cheeger-type inequalities for the second largest spectral gap from $1$ of the normalized Laplacian
entries.abstract: We study the second largest spectral gap from $1$ of the normalized Laplacian of a graph, a quantity that appears in the literature in connection with random walks, expander graphs, and Ramanujan graphs. We relate it to the classical Cheeger and dual Cheeger constants, and we introduce a new Cheeger-type constant admitting a probabilistic interpretation in terms of two-step random walks. For this constant, we establish sharp inequalities analogous to the classical Cheeger inequalities.

entries.name: Non-orbit 3-representation-finite symmetric algebras
entries.abstract: We construct two $3$-representation-finite symmetric algebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero that are not orbit algebras of repetitive categories. This answers a question of Darpö and Iyama in the negative.

entries.name: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
entries.abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for all sufficiently large $d$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

entries.name: Fast rates for the classification of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths
entries.abstract: In binary classification problems, plug-in classifiers can sometimes achieve faster excess risk rates than the underlying estimation rate. In this work, we study a supervised classification problem based on repeated independent observations of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, with both time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous drifts. We show that, under a suitable separation condition on the class-dependent drifts, a plug-in classifier attains an excess risk of quadratic order in the corresponding parametric or nonparametric estimation error. The theoretical approach utilizes the Wiener chaos representation and spectral theory to characterize the log-likelihood ratio as a quadratic form of Gaussian random variables, enabling a precise analysis of margin behaviour and deviation results. This extends the fast-rate results from classification problems with linear discriminant models and Gaussian white noise models to dynamical diffusion systems with Gaussian structure.

entries.name: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
entries.abstract: For $κ\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_κ$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circψ^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

entries.name: Higher cluster-tilting modules for blocks of finite groups
entries.abstract: We classify the $d$-representation-finite blocks of finite group algebras over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic. The main step is to show that if a block admits a $d$-cluster-tilting module with $d\geq3$, then it splits over the fraction field of the Witt vectors. This excludes generalized quaternion defect groups of order at least $16$.

entries.name: Degree Lower Bounds for Symmetric Boolean Functions: Breaking the Prime-Gap Barrier
entries.abstract: We prove that every nonconstant symmetric Boolean function on $n$ variables has exact real polynomial degree at least $n-O(n^{1/3}(\log n)^{2/3})$. This makes progress toward the conjecture of von zur Gathen and Roche that the degree is always at least $n-3$. The original prime-gap argument of von zur Gathen and Roche yields a degree deficit of $O(n^{0.525})$ using the theorem of Baker, Harman, and Pintz, or $O(n^{0.52})$ using an estimate claimed in a recent preprint. Our $\widetilde{O}(n^{1/3})$ bound on the degree deficit improves upon the $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{n})$ bound obtainable from the prime-gap approach, even assuming the Riemann hypothesis or Legendre's conjecture. Notably, our proof avoids prime-gap estimates entirely. The proof combines vanishing binomial moments with the arithmetic of linear recurrences. A quantitative form of the integer Hankel determinant method in the Pólya--Carlson theorem forces the function's values on a central interval of Hamming weights to satisfy a short rational recurrence. A second determinant argument bounds the number of characteristic roots near $-1$. Through the binomial transform, these roots can then be cancelled by a polynomial test of degree below the deficit. An integer annihilator and contour estimates make the test isolate the first failure of the recurrence, yielding a contradiction with the vanishing-moment conditions. If the recurrence agrees with the function on a sufficiently long interval, arithmetic height bounds instead force a bounded period, which is ruled out by a separate polynomial test. Every numbered result in the paper has been formally verified in Lean~4.

entries.name: Rigidity of Complete Self-shrinkers in Arbitrary Codimension
entries.abstract: We prove that a connected complete immersed self-shrinker in Euclidean space whose second fundamental form $h$ satisfies $|h|^2\le1$ is either a linear plane or a complete Riemannian covering of a generalized round cylinder. Neither properness nor polynomial volume growth is assumed. This proves the pinching classification conjectured by Cao and Li %[Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations \textbf{46} (2013)] in arbitrary codimension. The proof combines a localized maximum principle, a pointwise lower bound for the Bakry--Émery Ricci tensor, a weak Harnack inequality, and the convexity of the shrinker potential at the endpoint.

entries.name: Profile-Anchored Control: Velocity Shaping with Exact Disturbance Rejection and Transient-Free Replanning
entries.abstract: In many motion-control problems, how a target is approached matters as much as whether it is reached: speed and deceleration must stay within actuator, safety or comfort limits despite unknown loads and disturbances. Position-dependent velocity profiles provide a natural way to describe such requirements. We show that the square of such a profile can be used both to plan the motion and to construct the controller that executes it. Our main result, profile-anchored control with exact rejection (PACER), recovers the nominal motion after a finite time under an unknown gain and load, and then allows the profile to be replaced mid-motion without a transient. It combines a static law for scalar second-order systems with a dynamic law for first-order ones, used for disturbance rejection. The static law guarantees uniform global asymptotic stability under an unknown input gain with a known lower bound, and finite-time stability under local homogeneity, while the first-order law gives analogous guarantees under disturbances of bounded rate and provides the exact rejection in PACER. Replanning of a profile under speed, acceleration and jerk limits can be formulated as a convex program. The approach is illustrated on a simulated elevator.

entries.name: Comprehensive Gröbner Bases in Macaulay2
entries.abstract: Studying parameter-dependent polynomial systems often requires stratifying parameter space according to the algebraic or geometric properties of the specialised systems. Comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, which provide Gröbner bases valid under every specialisation, either uniformly or on specified regions of parameter space, are classical tools for studying polynomial ideals under specialisation. We introduce ComprehensiveGBs, a Macaulay2 package for computing comprehensive Gröbner bases and systems, either over the full parameter space or under specified parameter conditions. We describe its use and implementation, with examples involving Weierstrass cubics and graphs.

entries.name: Generic arm separation for planar percolation models
entries.abstract: Arm separation is an important technical tool in the study of critical and near-critical planar percolation systems. When combined with RSW estimates, it proves quasi-multiplicativity of arm-event probabilities, links the derivatives of different events and allows the identification of universal arm exponents. We provide a very generic statement of arm separation that applies to arbitrary planar percolation models. Our argument is based on exploring configurations conditioned on the existence of arms in such a way that "exposed" arms are revealed with positive probability. The exploration algorithm is independent of the percolation model and applies to all polychromatic arm events. As an application, we prove a strong arm-separation result for critical planar FK-percolation.

entries.name: Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
entries.abstract: We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.

entries.name: Neural Conditional Gaussian Model: Efficient Data Assimilation with Sequential Uncertainty Quantification for Nonlinear Dynamics
entries.abstract: Data assimilation (DA) in partially observed nonlinear systems requires repeated estimation of both hidden states and their uncertainty. Conventional nonlinear filtering can be computationally expensive and often relies on an explicit dynamical model. In this paper, we develop the Neural Conditional Gaussian Model (Neural CGM), a data-driven dynamical model that maps unobserved physical states into a learned latent space, where the dynamics of the latent states follow a conditional Gaussian structure. This structure allows closed-form DA updates in the latent space, while nonlinear encoder-decoder mappings retain the flexibility needed to represent complex dynamics in physical space. A key feature of Neural CGM is its treatment of uncertainty in DA. The latent posterior mean and covariance are mapped to the physical variables through a Gaussian decoder that combines local moment propagation with learned nonlinear corrections. The resulting physical-space posterior statistics depend on the sequentially updated latent distribution rather than on a separate post-processing estimate. The same statistics enter a Gaussian negative log-likelihood during training, so both the posterior mean and uncertainty affect the learned model. Because Neural CGM learns the dynamical model itself, it can also be used for state forecasting and simulation without explicit knowledge of the governing equations. Numerical experiments on benchmark nonlinear dynamical systems show accurate state estimation and forecasting while substantially reducing online assimilation cost relative to conventional nonlinear DA methods. Neural CGM is therefore suited to repeated state estimation, uncertainty quantification, and prediction from partial observations.

entries.name: Global existence versus blow-up for Fermi-Pasta-Ulam-Tsingou lattices
entries.abstract: This paper investigates the global behavior of infinite nonlinear lattices. In particular, for the Fermi--Pasta--Ulam--Tsingou-$α$ lattice (FPUT-$α$), we show global existence for small initial data via a region-based approach, and prove blow-up for negative energy and some positive energy, given appropriate conditions on the initial momentum and dispersion. Moreover, we extend these results to the nonlinear Klein-Gordon (DNKG) equation and nonlinear wave (DNW) equation. \

entries.name: Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions
entries.abstract: We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.

entries.name: A constructive inverse for the Jordan-von Neuman operator on abelian groups
entries.abstract: For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.

entries.name: Preventing cycles in Lotka--Volterra systems
entries.abstract: We study cycles of heteroclinic connections between equilibria of Lotka--Volterra systems with negative self-interactions. We prove that generalized strict diagonal dominance makes the invasion, connection, and weak graphs acyclic for every intrinsic growth vector. No hyperbolicity assumption is needed, and the associated semiflow is gradient with respect to its equilibria. For the broader class of Volterra--Lyapunov stable matrices, we show that two equilibria are joined by a heteroclinic connection exactly when the species that enter have positive invasion rates at the source and the species that leave have nonpositive invasion rates at the target. We show by examples that the three graphs can differ, that the dominance threshold is sharp, and that generalized dominance is not necessary for acyclicity. We also give a quantitative criterion for cycle exclusion in terms of the symmetric and skew parts of a weighted interaction matrix.

entries.name: A new algorithmic approach for finding flat minima: critically damped Polyak stepsizes
entries.abstract: We present a new adaptive stepsize rule that biases gradient descent toward flatter minima in both theory and practice, and establish the first uniform-in-time guarantees for both sharpness and loss reduction for a broad class of locally quadratic objectives. Our critically damped Polyak (CDP) stepsizes multiply the classical Polyak rule by $4$ and a mild damping factor. The factor $4$ is critical in that it produces equioscillations around the manifold of minimizers $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order. Damping provably drives convergence to $\mathcal{M}$. CDP thus operates at the edge of stability by adapting its stepsizes to local curvature. Once the loss is small, its projected iterates follow gradient descent on $\log{λ_1(\nabla^2 \mathcal{L})}$ along $\mathcal{M}$ to leading order, paralleling the flatness bias of normalized gradient descent (Arora et al., 2022). Unlike normalized gradient descent, CDP step lengths shrink with the distance to $\mathcal{M}$, enabling convergence to an interpolating solution that locally minimizes sharpness at finite learning rate. We establish our theory for a broad class of non-negative losses with locally quadratic Morse-Bott structure near $\mathcal{M}$, capturing regular interpolation regimes in smooth overparameterized neural networks. Empirically, CDP stepsizes produce a flattening effect similar to that of Sharpness-Aware Minimization (SAM, Foret et al., 2021), reducing sharpness even in settings beyond our theory, including nonlinear teacher-student networks and fine-tuning of pre-trained LLMs.

entries.name: Nonlinear Fourier series
entries.abstract: We survey aspects of nonlinear Fourier series as presented in the 2026 Brouwer lecture by the second author. The fast nonlinear Fourier expansion mentioned in the lecture is further elaborated in joint work with the first author.

entries.name: Spectral asymptotics for vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators
entries.abstract: We consider vector-valued magnetic Schrödinger operators $-Δ_{a} +V$ with magnetic potential ${a}\in C^2(\mathbb{R}^d;\mathbb{R}^d)$ and electric potential $V$ given by a symmetric and positive semidefinite $m\times m$ matrix-valued function whose entries belong to $L^1_{\rm loc}(\mathbb{R}^d)$. Assuming that $\|\operatorname{curl} {a}(\cdot)\|\operatorname{Id}_{\mathbb{R}^m} + V$ belongs to a certain matrix reverse Hölder class, we characterize necessary and sufficient conditions under which the spectrum of $-Δ_{a} +V$ is discrete, and study the eigenvalue asymptotics and exponential decay of eigenfunctions.

entries.name: Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
entries.abstract: We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.

entries.name: Local Clustering Tests and Botnet Localization in Sparse Random Geometric Networks
entries.abstract: We use local clustering to test for botnets in sparse random geometric networks. Under the null hypothesis, the vertices are independent uniform points on a fixed-dimensional torus, with edges determined by a distance threshold. Under the alternative, an unknown set of vertices ignores the geometry and connects independently with the same marginal edge probability. Every prescribed vertex has the same marginal binomial degree law under both hypotheses, so its degree alone carries no information. Triangle closure, however, distinguishes the two models. Under the null, conditional on a degree of at least two, the local clustering coefficient has exact mean $C_d>0$, a known constant that depends only on the dimension. Under the alternative, the corresponding mean is $p_n$ for a bot. For a non-bot, the corresponding mixture mean converges to $C_d$ when the botnet size is $o(n)$. We prove non-asymptotic concentration bounds, an exponential bound on the worst-case risk of a scan test, and exact-support recovery. For every deterministic sequence $1\leq k_n=o(n)$, if $μ_n=(n-1)p_n$ satisfies $μ_n/\log n\to\infty$, the local rule recovers the botnet with probability tending to one, uniformly over all label sets of size $k_n$. The proof combines geometric U-statistics, bounded differences on random neighborhoods, and a stability bound showing that genuine vertices retain their geometric clustering when bots form only a vanishing fraction of their neighbors. The test does not use the latent positions. The theorem assumes that the model parameters are known, although $C_d$ can instead be estimated consistently. In the high-expected-degree regime, the rule also works for a single bot.

entries.name: Nondefective lifts of stationary discs and the 2-jet determination problem
entries.abstract: We introduce a natural notion of defect for lifts of stationary discs attached to a CR nondegenerate submanifold $M \subset \mathbb{C}^N$ of codimension $d$. We prove that the existence of a nondefective lift of a stationary disc implies that germs of CR automorphisms of $M$ are uniquely determined by their $2$-jet. We emphasize that, in particular, this unifies all previously known results on this question.

entries.name: The Rate of Convergence of Empirical $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein Distances
entries.abstract: We study empirical convergence rates for $(p,q)$-Gromov-Wasserstein (GW) distances $D_{p,q}$ for arbitrary real exponents $p>0$ and $q\ge1$. Let $μ$ and $ν$ be probability measures on compact metric spaces $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$, and let $\widehatμ_n$ and $\widehatν_m$ be their empirical measures, constructed from independent i.i.d. samples of sizes $n$ and $m$. If the spaces $\mathcal{X},\,\mathcal{Y}$ are compact subsets of the Euclidean spaces $\mathbb{R}^{d_x}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{d_y}$, respectively, we obtain an upper bound of order $(n\wedge m)^{-(p\wedge2)/((d_x\wedge d_y)\vee 2(p\wedge2))}$ on the plug-in error of $D_{p,q}^p(\widehatμ_n,\widehatν_m)$ in expectation, up to a logarithmic factor at the critical dimension $d_x\wedge d_y=2(p\wedge2)$. On Euclidean balls, this rate is sharp up to the logarithmic factor. More generally, we show that the same upper bound holds when one space is a compact subset of a complete, connected $d$-dimensional Riemannian manifold and the other has polynomial covering numbers, with $d_x\wedge d_y$ replaced by $d$. Earlier works on $(2,2)$-GW, $(2,1)$-GW and other even-order cases rely on variational representations of GW distances that are specific to their exponents. We instead reduce the plug-in error to an analysis of empirical processes through local duality, which may be of independent interest.

entries.name: Existence and uniqueness for a coagulation-transport equation
entries.abstract: This paper establishes the existence, uniqueness, and regularity of weak solutions to a class of nonlinear coagulation-transport equations describing the asymptotic dynamics of multispecies coalescent processes. The model captures the multi-scale ancestral lineage decay governed by an autonomous drift field, coupled with a time-inhomogeneous quadratic coagulation term parameterized by the initial population mass. By utilizing the metric structure of probability measures, we demonstrate that any weak solution satisfies a unique mild representation formula dictated by the transport semigroup. This characterization allows us to construct a unified narrative where existence, uniqueness, and moment preservation are proved directly through a contractive fixed-point argument in the space of finite Radon measures.

entries.name: Lyapunov Theory for Output-to-State Stability of Nonlinear Infinite-Dimensional Systems
entries.abstract: For a broad class of nonlinear infinite-dimensional systems with outputs, we show that output-to-state stability (OSS) is equivalent to the existence of a coercive OSS Lyapunov function in implication form. While establishing this equivalence, we prove that OSS is equivalent to uniform global asymptotic stability modulo output, relate these properties to the vanishing output vanishing state property, and highlight new challenges that do not arise in the nonlinear finite-dimensional or linear infinite-dimensional settings. The results are illustrated by a nonlinear reaction-diffusion system with a nonlinear output map.

entries.name: Super quantum groups of divided powers à la Lusztig
entries.abstract: We construct super analogues of the quantum groups of divided powers introduced by Lusztig. We call them super analogues because the Lie-theoretical data governing their structure is comparable to that of contragredient Lie superalgebras. Indeed, we show that they admit PBW-type bases parametrized by root systems of super type, and that they also have Lusztig isomorphisms giving a representation of the corresponding Weyl groupoids. Moreover, we prove that our super objects are equipped with a Frobenius-type morphism whose kernel is the Drinfeld double of a finite-dimensional Nichols algebra of super type, a super analogue of Lusztig's small quantum group, and whose cokernel is the enveloping algebra of the semisimple Lie algebra determined by the Cartan roots of the Nichols algebra. We carry out our construction within the framework of Nichols algebras of diagonal type, specifically, those whose braiding is obtained by specializing at a root of unity. This allows us to consider a divided power integral form inside a large quantum group of De Concini--Kac--Procesi type and then, via specialization, obtain our desired object.

entries.name: Hypergraph Hajnal-Szemerédi
entries.abstract: A seminal result of Hajnal and Szemerédi from 1970 asserts that every graph on $n$ vertices with $q\;|\;n$ and minimum degree at least $\Big(1-\frac{1}{q}\Big)n$ admits a $K_q$-factor (a collection of vertex-disjoint copies of $K_q$ spanning all vertices). There has been sustained interest in extending this result to hypergraph $K_q^r$-factors. For general $q$ and $r$, Lu and Székely in 2007 showed that every large enough, $r$-graph $G$ with $q\mid v(G)$ and $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1- \frac{c}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ admits a $K_q^r$-factor (where $c$ is a constant depending on $r$ but not $q$), and there have been various subsequent improvements to the constant (but not the order) of this bound over the ensuing decades. Meanwhile, results from codegree Turán theory show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left(1 - \frac{c \cdot \log q}{q^{r-1}} \right)v(G)$ is necessary. Surprisingly, our main result shows that the order of this upper bound is not correct and, in fact, the codegree $K_q^r$-factor threshold is much closer to this codegree Turán theory bound. In particular, we show that $δ_{r-1}(G) \ge \left( 1-c\cdot \frac{\log^{1-1/(r-1)}q}{q^{r-1}}\right)v(G)$ suffices for the existence of a $K_q^r$-factor. Our key contribution is showing the same is true for the fractional threshold. Inspired by the first and fourth author's recent proof of the Nash-Williams' Conjecture, we accomplish this by combining a linear programming framework with ideas from discharging. Additionally, we establish a technical result about finding large independent sets in sparse, non-uniform hypergraphs, which may be of independent interest.

entries.name: Simple Private Noisy SGD is Minimax-Optimal under Population Strong Convexity
entries.abstract: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is at the center of modern machine learning and is known to be statistically minimax-optimal in many regression settings, e.g., for convex Generalized Linear Models (GLMs). Yet, it is unknown whether its simplest differentially private Noisy SGD counterpart fulfills similar favorable guarantees even on strongly convex losses. We resolve this question affirmatively. We upper bound the parameter estimation error for a single pass of Noisy SGD with a fixed stepsize schedule and constant batch sizes on smooth and strongly convex Lipschitz losses over a compact convex domain under Renyi DP. Specialized to strongly convex GLMs, our error bounds match minimax lower bounds we derive based on the Score Attack framework. In particular, this provides the first minimax-optimal rate for Noisy SGD in private logistic regression, avoiding poly-logarithmic terms present in existing results. Our analysis is versatile as it relies on standard convex analysis and establishes the same rates in expectation and with high probability.

entries.name: Remark on Kobayashi's conjecture: a volume Schwarz lemma
entries.abstract: This remark offers an expository reconstruction of OpenAI's proof of Kobayashi's ampleness conjecture for compact Kähler manifolds, together with new results. We extract a volume Schwarz lemma for extremal discs and derive a pointwise volume comparison: the volume form of a Kähler metric with $\mathrm{Ric}(ω)\ge-ω$ is bounded below by an intrinsic volume form built from the Kähler--Einstein metrics of pseudoconvex domains containing the Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix. As a consequence, if a compact Kähler manifold $X$ has nef canonical bundle and its Kobayashi--Royden indicatrix is bounded at some point, then $X$ is of general type.

entries.name: Anytime-valid inference for time series via self-normalization
entries.abstract: We develop a self-normalized approach to constructing asymptotic confidence sequences for a broad class of parameters of stationary time series under weak dependence. Our theory covers nonlinear marginal parameters, including quantiles, expectiles and expected shortfall, as well as autoregressive coefficients. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of self-normalization to construct asymptotic confidence sequences for time series. A key advantage is that the construction avoids direct estimation of the long-run variance, which can be particularly challenging for nonlinear parameters under serial dependence. Following an initial burn-in period of length $m$, confidence intervals are released sequentially, with simultaneous coverage over all subsequent times converging to $1-α$ as $m\to\infty$. We propose two sequential self-normalizers with complementary statistical and computational advantages. The forward construction uses only the history of sequential parameter estimates, leading to minimal computational overhead. The three-block construction typically yields narrower confidence sequences and is compatible with the optimal law-of-the-iterated-logarithm width rate. Together, these constructions extend the benefits of self-normalization to sequential inference under dependence. We investigate their finite-sample performance through simulations and illustrate their use in Markov chain Monte Carlo output analysis in the supplementary appendix.

entries.name: Large $k$-cross-free families
entries.abstract: Two subsets $A,B$ of a finite set $X$ are crossing if $A\cap B$, $A\setminus B$, $B\setminus A$, and $X\setminus(A\cup B)$ are all nonempty. A family is $k$-cross-free if it contains no $k$ pairwise crossing members. We construct such families on $n$ elements of size $(\frac{1}{3}+o(1))kn\log k$, where the asymptotic is taken as $k$ tends to infinity and is uniform over all integers $n\ge k$. This disproves the uniform $O(kn)$ bound conjectured by Karzanov and Lomonosov. Our construction consists of cyclic intervals with at most one point deleted, together with their complements. We also prove an $O(kn\log k)$ upper bound for $k$-cross-free families closed under all cyclic shifts of a fixed cyclic ordering of the ground set.

entries.name: Minimization of free energy in a Poisson--Boltzmann problem
entries.abstract: In this paper, we study a mathematical model in which an ionic solution composed of several types of spherical ions is confined between two uniformly charged parallel planes. The ion concentrations at equilibrium, determined by the interplay between thermal and electrostatic effects, are obtained by minimizing the free energy of the system. The resulting minimization problem is infinite-dimensional, and we prove the existence and uniqueness of its solution by means of a norm-convergence direct method based on the Banach--Saks property of the space in which the problem is posed. The existence proof is technically challenging because the functional to be minimized is not coercive in general. Three illustrative problems are considered and solved numerically.

entries.name: Pathwise uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with a $3/4$-Hölder diffusion coefficient
entries.abstract: For every $γ\in[3/4,1]$, we prove pathwise uniqueness and strong existence for the stochastic heat equation on $\mathbb{R}$ with space-time white noise, Lipschitz drift, and a diffusion coefficient locally $γ$-Hölder under suitable growth bounds. The result settles the critical case $γ=3/4$ left open by Mueller, Mytnik and Perkins. The proof is based on a newly developed short-time linear comparison method. On each short interval, we compare the difference of two solutions with an auxiliary linear process. An expected weighted $L^1$ bound independent of the noise multiplier, together with a vanishing sum of approximation errors, yields pathwise uniqueness. The method may also apply to other SPDEs admitting analogous linear comparison and stochastic convolution estimates.

entries.name: A time-domain adversarial example demonstrating the failure of $H^1$ elements in $a$-$φ$ electromagnetic simulation
entries.abstract: Frequently, $H^1$ continuous finite elements are used in computational electromagnetics despite it being widely known that such an interpolation is not guaranteed to furnish reliable approximations of solutions to general initial/boundary value problems. It is mathematically more natural to use $H(\text{Curl})$ elements (edge elements) than $H^1$ elements, since the former form part of a discrete complex that respects the differential-geometric structure of Maxwell's equations while the latter do not. However, most work discussing the failure of $H^1$ elements for electromagnetics is esoteric and concrete examples demonstrating the clear advantage of edge elements are generally restricted to quasi-static, frequency-domain, or eigenvalue problems. In this work, we summarize essential facts regarding $H^1$ and $H(\text{Curl})$ elements and present a physically feasible yet intentionally adversarial time-domain eddy-current example demonstrating the failure of gauge-penalized $H^1$ elements in an $a$-$φ$ formulation compared to gauge-free mixed scalar/edge $H^1/H(\text{Curl})$ elements. The results indicate that edge elements can be used to furnish reasonable results for general loading conditions, whereas penalized $H^1$ elements fail (e.g., converge to an incorrect state) even with mesh refinement.

entries.name: Multiplicative Sidon basis
entries.abstract: For a $h \ge 2$ integer a sequence of positive integers $A$ is called asymptotic basis of order $h$ if every sufficiently large positive integer $n$ can be written as a sum of $h$ elements of $A$. We say a sequence of positive integers $A$ is a multiplicative Sidon sequence if all the products of two elements of the sequence $A$ are distinct. In this paper we prove the existence of a multiplicative Sidon set which is an asymptotic basis of order 2 by using the probabilistic method.

entries.name: Edge cuts of bounded degree in sparse graphs
entries.abstract: Every simple graph on $n \ge 2$ vertices with at most $2n-2$ edges can be split into two nonempty parts with at most two crossing edges at each vertex. For $d \ge 3$ we bound the minimum number of edges in an n-vertex graph without a d-cut.

entries.name: Topological notions of Shadowing under Semi-Conjugacy
entries.abstract: We study various notions of shadowing and investigate whether they are preserved under semi-conjugacy and inverse limits. In particular, we study Inverse shadowing, $H$-shadowing, Periodic shadowing, Ramsey shadowing, Density shadowing and Ergodic shadowing.

entries.name: Optimal Control in Pairs Trading with Negative-Power Utility
entries.abstract: We solve a finite-horizon consumption and investment problem in a pairs trading model with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck spread and utility $U(x)=-x^{-γ}$, $γ>0$. Linearizing the Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation gives explicit formulas for the value function and the optimal feedback control. A budget inequality and concavity verify optimality over all admissible strategies with nonnegative wealth on every finite horizon, without Novikov's condition. Under the optimal feedback, wealth and consumption admit deterministic upper bounds when the interest rate $r$ is at most the mean-reversion rate $κ$. If $r>κ$, each exceeds any prescribed level with positive probability at every time after the start. If $r>\sqrt{2+γ} κ$, there is an explicit critical horizon at and beyond which expected terminal wealth is infinite, while optimal expected utility is finite. When the critical time falls before maturity, expected wealth at that time is finite exactly when the initial spread is zero. We also show that the suprema of the negative powers of optimal wealth and consumption are integrable on every finite horizon exactly for orders $0<m\le 1+γ$.

entries.name: On Romik's rationality conjectures for critical percolation
entries.abstract: The completely packed $O(1)$ loop model can be viewed as an interface representation of critical bond percolation on the square lattice. We consider submatching events, which prescribe how these interfaces pair finitely many consecutive boundary points. Romik's rationality conjectures predict that the probabilities of these events on the semi-infinite cylinder are given by specific rational functions, which even become dyadic rationals in the half-plane limit. We derive explicit Pfaffian formulae for the probability of $k$ nested arches on the semi-infinite cylinder of circumference $2N$, valid for $k<N$. We deduce that these probabilities are rational functions of $N$ and, by taking the limit $N\to\infty$, that the corresponding half-plane probabilities remain rational. This establishes key aspects of Romik's conjectures. Our proof uses identities of Fonseca and Zinn-Justin, derived through the qKZ formalism, which express these probabilities as ratios of enumeration numbers for totally symmetric self-complementary plane partitions (TSSCPPs). These plane partitions admit a dimer representation, allowing us to apply Kasteleyn theory. We evaluate the resulting hypergeometric sum using Zeilberger's and Gosper's algorithms and then take the half-plane limit $N\to\infty$. Along the way, we derive a somewhat simplified expression for the inverse Kasteleyn matrix entries (encoding correlations in TSSCPPs) of Ayyer and Chhita, which might be of independent interest.

entries.name: Global regularity in optimal transportation under the A3w condition
entries.abstract: We prove global $C^{2,α}$ and $W^{2,p}$ estimates for potentials in optimal transportation under A3w condition. The cost satisfies condition A3w, and the domains are mutually uniformly $c$-convex with $C^2$ boundaries. We prove global $W^{2,p}$ estimates for positive continuous densities and we obtain global $C^{2,α}$ estimates for positive $C^α$ densities.

entries.name: Optimal Scheduling of Multi-Site AI Data Centers in Day-Ahead Markets
entries.abstract: AI data centers are among the fastest-growing loads on the power grid, and their flexibility is increasingly sought by grid operators. Using it requires a model that links what an operator controls, namely GPU power caps, job timing and job placement, to the power drawn at each site and the electricity prices it faces. This paper develops such a framework for a multi-site AI data-center fleet. It represents GPU power-cap levels; deferrable jobs with deadlines and inference with response-time headroom; and site facility power, and casts the fleet schedule as a linear program solved on day-ahead prices. A year-long simulation on 2025 California Independent System Operator (CAISO) day-ahead prices in three data-center markets demonstrates the framework. Coordinated scheduling lowers the fleet's energy cost by 6.3% at equal work. Four operating modes, each adding one capability, split this saving into efficient GPU operation that needs no price signal, price response in time, and routing work between sites.

entries.name: Stochastic counterpart of Nesterov's method for sampling and provable non-acceleration of samplers with heavy-ball structure
entries.abstract: Polyak's heavy-ball method and Nesterov's method are two momentum-based methods that have inspired many optimization techniques used in applied fields, including machine learning. Momentum also provides a connection with sampling, and interestingly, many kinetic Langevin samplers reduce to the heavy-ball recurrence when velocity is eliminated and noise is removed. This observation motivates a natural question: what is the corresponding sampler for Nesterov's method? We propose a sampler whose deterministic part is exactly Nesterov's recurrence, driven by temporally correlated Gaussian noise and requires one new gradient evaluation per step. Noise correlation provides $\mathcal{O}(h^2)$ bias for smooth observables. We establish geometric ergodicity for possibly non-convex potentials. For strongly convex potentials with Lipschitz continuous gradients, we obtain contraction rates and show that, up to an additive constant, the energy decays at a rate of order $κ^{-1/2}$, where $κ$ is the condition number. For Gaussian targets, we show that relaxation has square-root dependence on $κ$. We further prove that any sampler based on heavy-ball dynamics with additive noise cannot achieve accelerated convergence uniformly over the class of strongly convex functions. Finally, we compare the proposed sampler with OBABO, BAOAB, HMC, MALA, BPS, and NUTS in numerical experiments and demonstrate the better performance of proposed sampler.

entries.name: Trimmed Branching Brownian Motion with Discontinuous Drift
entries.abstract: We consider a system of branching Brownian particles on the real line with bounded, possibly discontinuous drift $b$, and with a selection rule that removes one particle from the most crowded cells of a uniform partition of the line at each branching event so that the number of particles is preserved. As the number of particles tends to infinity, with the cell size tending to zero (sufficiently slowly), we prove convergence in probability of the empirical measure process to a deterministic limit characterized by the parabolic free obstacle problem $$\partial_tu=\tfrac12\partial_{xx}u-\partial_x(bu)+u-β.$$ Here the density $u$ has unit mass. Disintegrating the removal measure $β$ as $β_t(\mathrm{d} x)\mathrm{d} t$, the probability measure $β_t$ is supported on the spatial maximizers of $u(t,\cdot)$ for a.e. $t$. We establish existence and uniqueness of weak solutions in a suitable class of continuous densities, extending earlier results about this PDE to discontinuous drifts. We then consider an inverse problem: Given a target removal measure, find a drift for which the PDE admits a stationary solution with that removal measure. We show that this problem is solvable for every compactly supported Borel probability measure.

entries.name: Existence and Uniqueness of Mild Solutions to Rough Stochastic Partial Differential Equations driven by Fractional Brownian Motion with Hurst Index $H > 1/4$
entries.abstract: In this paper we prove a theorem on the unique solvability of the Cauchy problem for a stochastic partial differential equation driven by the fractional Brownian motion with Hurst index $H>\frac{1}{4}$.

entries.name: Amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves and applications
entries.abstract: We prove amplitude dependent wave envelope type estimates for moment curves in arbitrary dimensions. The proof uses the sharp square function estimates of Maldague and Guth-Maldague. As an application, we establish sharp small cap decoupling inequalities for the moment curve in every dimension $n\geq4$. This proves the conjecture of Demeter-Guth-Wang on exponential sums in all dimensions.

entries.name: Equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for congruence subgroups of level 2
entries.abstract: The modular properties of holomorphic Eisenstein series for $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and its congruence subgroups do not carry over to their primitives. Instead, the transformation of iterated Eisenstein integrals under congruence subgroups of level $N$ introduces inhomogeneous terms comprising (among others) cyclotomic multiple zeta values of level $N$. We combine iterated Eisenstein integrals for the congruence subgroups of level $N=2$ of arbitrary iteration depth with their complex conjugates and (single-valued) level-2 cyclotomic multiple zeta values such that they define non-holomorphic modular forms. Our construction of these so-called equivariant iterated Eisenstein integrals for $Γ(2)$ and $Γ_0(2)$ proceeds at the level of generating series that take values in an infinite-dimensional (pro-unipotent) Lie group and closely follow Brown's analogous construction in the $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ case. The required insertions of cyclotomic multiple zeta values are controlled by zeta generators for level 2 that normalise the corresponding (pro-nilpotent) Lie algebra of the generating series and whose Lie-bracket relations we determine systematically. Upon restriction to Eisenstein series of modular weight~2, we recover single-valued multiple polylogarithms on the genus 0 modular curve $Γ(2)\backslash \mathbb{H}$.

entries.name: A Tutorial on Complementarity-Based Contact Models for Robotics
entries.abstract: Simulating rigid-body dynamics with contact is fundamental to robotics, from motion synthesis and control to mechanism design. Many widely used simulators rely on cone complementarity formulations, whose physical assumptions and numerical solution require substantial background. While excellent surveys, monographs, and course notes exist, they mostly address computational mechanics or computer graphics or document a single simulator. To the best of our knowledge, a self-contained pedagogical treatment for robotics, bringing these formulations and their solvers together with complete derivations and a unified notation, does not yet exist. This tutorial addresses this gap by connecting rigid-body dynamics, conic optimization, and frictional contact. In particular, we explain how complementarity conditions encode non-penetration and frictional dissipation, determining separation, sticking, and sliding without prescribed contact modes. We distinguish equivalent transcriptions from convex relaxations, showing how the latter can introduce artifacts such as lift-off and creep. We examine the existence and uniqueness of motion and contact forces, including the solver's role in selecting among multiple solutions. We then compare first-order and Newton-based methods, explain regularization and proximal strategies, and discuss trade-offs between computational cost, robustness, and physical fidelity. Connections to widely used simulators, optimal control, and differentiable simulation help readers interpret simulation results, choose suitable formulations and solvers, and develop their own contact dynamics routines.

entries.name: Additive Fréchet Regression for Random Objects
entries.abstract: Regression analysis for complex data taking values in a general metric space has gained increasing attention in recent years, particularly in the context of Fréchet regression with Euclidean predictors $\mathbb{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{p}$. However, local Fréchet regression, while more flexible than global Fréchet regression, suffers from the curse of dimensionality for the case of multivariate predictors. To address this issue while maintaining model flexibility, we introduce a framework of additive structured nonparametric regression when responses are situated in a general metric space. Overcoming the challenge of the lack of vector space structure in general metric spaces where the responses reside requires a novel approach that incorporates the additive structure via projection operators. This leads to a unified framework of additive regression for a wide range of response types, including one-dimensional distributions in Wasserstein space, network data represented by graph Laplacians and spherical data equipped with geodesic distances, among others. We establish pointwise and uniform consistency, including convergence rates, for the proposed additive Fréchet regression estimators, using smooth backfitting. The practical utility of this additive model is demonstrated through applications to brain connectivity network analysis using resting-state fMRI data and distributional physical activity data.

entries.name: Permanence and $144$-periodicity of $x_{153,3}$ in the stable stems at the prime three
entries.abstract: The class $x_{153,3}$ lies in stable degree $153$ and filtration $3$ on the algebraic starting page of the $3$-primary Adams--Novikov spectral sequence of the sphere. We show that it survives and begins a family with period $144$, answering both parts of a question of Carrick and Davies. A comparison with periodic topological modular forms and a bound on the possible differential targets prove permanence. A divisibility calculation for the mod-$3$ Moore spectrum supplies a lift to a finite spectrum with a degree-$144$ self-map. The resulting iterates have nonzero image in the height-two detector of Carrick and Davies.

entries.name: Quasipolynomial pyjamas
entries.abstract: The ``pyjama stripe" $E(\varepsilon)$ is the set of all complex numbers whose real part lies within $\varepsilon$ of the nearest integer. The Pyjama Problem asks whether, for each $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some union of finitely many rotations of $E(\varepsilon)$ about the origin that covers the plane. This was answered in the affirmative by Manners. Kravitz and Leng subsequently showed that $\exp(\exp(\exp(\varepsilon^{-O(1)})))$ rotations suffice. In this paper, we prove an upper bound of \[\exp((\log \varepsilon^{-1})^{50000})\] rotations. We also show that at least $(π/2 + 0.003 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$ rotations are necessary, improving upon the natural lower bound of $(π/2 + o(1))\varepsilon^{-1}$.

entries.name: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
entries.abstract: We show that any area-preserving $C^r$-diffeomorphism of a two-dimensional surface displaying an elliptic fixed point can be $C^r$-perturbed to one exhibiting a chaotic island whose metric entropy is positive, for every $1\le r\le \infty$. This proves a conjecture of Herman stating that the identity map of the disk can be $C^\infty$-perturbed to a conservative diffeomorphism with positive metric entropy. This implies also that the Chirikov standard map for large and small parameter values can be $C^\infty$-approximated by a conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy (a weak version of Sinai's positive metric entropy conjecture). Finally, this sheds light onto a Herman's question on the density of $C^r$-conservative diffeomorphisms displaying a positive metric entropy: we show the existence of a dense set formed by conservative diffeomorphism which either are weakly stable (so, conjecturally, uniformly hyperbolic) or display a chaotic island of positive metric entropy.

entries.name: Notes on modules of finite injective dimension
entries.abstract: Motivated by Bass' conjecture, we study finitely generated modules of finite injective dimension and the additional constraints they impose on the ambient ring. Beyond ensuring the Cohen--Macaulay property, the presence of such modules enforces further conditions on the ring, including reducedness, normality, being an integral domain, and various singularity conditions such as complete intersection, Gorenstein, and beyond. This continues to detect non-singularity as well. We also address the reflexivity (and also torsionlessness) of modules with finite injective dimension and show that this forces the ring to be quasi-normal. In the same vein, we investigate the injective dimension of tensor products and endomorphism rings. Finally, we study the behavior of R when high syzygies of ksurject onto a non-zero R-module of finite injective dimension.

entries.name: On the cone conjecture for pairs of large Kodaira dimension
entries.abstract: In this paper, by running the minimal model program and considering the anti-canonical fibration, we prove the Morrison-Kawamata cone conjecture for klt Calabi-Yau pairs $(X,Δ)$ such that the Iitaka dimension $κ(X,-K_X)$ is at least $\dim X - 2$.

entries.name: Jordan-Hölder property for shifted quantum affine algebras
entries.abstract: We prove that finite length representations of shifted quantum affine algebras in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ are stable by fusion product. This implies that in the topological Grothendieck ring $K_0(\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}})$ the Grothendieck group of finite length representations forms a non-topological subring. We also conjecture this subring is isomorphic to the cluster algebra discovered in arXiv:2401.04616. In the course of our proofs, we establish that any simple representation in category $\mathcal{O}^{\mathrm{sh}}$ descends to a truncation, for certain truncation parameters as conjectured in arXiv:2010.06996 in terms of Langlands dual $q$-characters.

entries.name: Unimodality and Cluster Algebras from Surfaces
entries.abstract: We prove that the rank polynomial of the lattice of order ideals of a loop fence poset is unimodal. This poset arises as the poset of join-irreducibles in the lattice of good matchings of loop graphs associated with notched arcs. Equivalently, such polynomials can be obtained by evaluating all coefficient variables in an F-polynomial at a single variable q. We also conclude that the rank polynomial of any tagged arc, whether plain or notched, is not only unimodal but also satisfies a symmetry condition known as almost interlacing. Furthermore, when the lamination consists of a single curve, the cluster expansion-evaluated by setting all cluster variables to 1 and all coefficient variables to q-is also unimodal. We conjecture that polynomials in this case are log-concave.

entries.name: A case of the dijoin conjecture on inverting oriented graphs
entries.abstract: For an oriented graph $D$, the inversion of $X\subseteq V(D)$ in $D$ is the graph obtained by reversing the orientation of all arcs with both ends in $X$. The inversion number $\mathrm{inv}(D)$ is the minimum number of inversions needed to obtain an acyclic oriented graph. We show that the dijoin conjecture of Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet, that $\mathrm{inv}(D_1\rightarrow D_2)=\mathrm{inv}(D_1)+\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$, is true in the case where $\mathrm{inv}(D_1)=2$ and $\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$ is even. We also characterise the cases $\mathrm{inv}(D_1)=2$ and $\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$ odd, for which the conjecture does and does not hold. We then go on to show a similar result for n-joins, in doing so we prove a conjecture of Alon, Powierski, Savery, Scott and Wilmer. Our proofs build on the idea of tournament minimum rank, introduced by Behague, Johnston, Morrison and Ogden.

entries.name: A nonvanishing criterion and families of counterexamples to the motivic Peterson conjecture
entries.abstract: The motivic Peterson conjecture asks whether the numerical condition forcing classical polynomial indecomposables to vanish has the same consequence in motivic cohomology. Kameko disproved this assertion by constructing a family of non-hit monomials. To determine all linear relations among the projected classes of these monomials, we compute the image of the motivic hit subspace under a projection onto their span: it consists precisely of the combinations whose coefficients sum to zero. Explicit Bockstein preimages establish the reverse inclusion, showing that no further linear relations hold and yielding a nonvanishing criterion. A binary calculation then produces infinitely many counterexamples for each fixed difference of at least three between the number of variables and the exterior degree.

entries.name: Oort's conjecture on automorphisms of generic supersingular abelian varieties
entries.abstract: We prove Oort's conjecture that generically on the supersingular locus of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of genus g and in characteristic p, the automorphism group of the universal principally polarized abelian variety consists only of $\pm 1$, unless g=2, 3 or 4 and p=2. On the way, we provide an explicit description of the a=1-locus in the Rapoport-Zink space of principally polarized supersingular p-divisible groups of any dimension g. We also prove analogous results for generic automorphism groups on moduli spaces of supersingular p-divisible groups with and without polarization.

entries.name: The maximum Cox complexity of a Fano-type variety and the Mukai conjecture
entries.abstract: We define an intrinsic invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(\cdot)$, the maximum Cox complexity, of Fano-type varieties $X$. We prove $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$ and $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)=0$ if and only if $X$ is toric. We then apply this invariant to the Mukai conjecture, which characterises powers of projective spaces among smooth Fano varieties in terms of $\dim(X)$, the Picard number $ρ(X)$, and the Fano index $i(X)$. All klt Fano varieties $X$ canonically embed into a projective toric variety $Z$ via their Cox ring. When $Z$ is smooth, we call $X$ ambiently smooth. We prove the Mukai conjecture for ambiently smooth Fano varieties by establishing the stronger inequality: $\dim(X)+ρ(X)-i(X)ρ(X)\geqγ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\geq 0$. Notably, 45% of the deformation families of smooth Fano threefolds have an ambiently smooth member. For a Fano-type variety $X$, the invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$ is defined using coefficient sums of anticanonical divisors supported on the divisors corresponding to minimal homogeneous generators of the Cox ring. Our proof proceeds by reducing the Cox ring to positive characteristic, using strong F-regularity to obtain the coefficients of an anticanonical divisor, and the F-pure threshold to establish the nonnegativity of $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$.

entries.name: Oddomorphisms, Split-Off Minors, and the Strong Roberson Conjecture
entries.abstract: We show that the existence of an oddomorphism from a graph $F$ to a graph $G$ does not imply that $G$ is a minor of $F$. This answers a question posed by Roberson (2026) and shows that the CFI graphs cannot be used to prove the Strong Roberson Conjecture. Additionally, we introduce the concept of a split-off minor and show that the existence of an oddomorphism from $F$ to $G$ implies that $G$ is a split-off minor of $F$. Consequently, every class that is closed under taking split-off minors and disjoint unions is homomorphism distinguishing closed. The split-off minor relation is the first minor-like structural relation shown to have this property, marking a meaningful advancement in our understanding of the interaction between structural graph containment and homomorphism indistinguishability relations.

entries.name: Real morsifications via the trace map
entries.abstract: We prove that every reduced real plane curve singularity admits a real morsification. This settles a question of A'Campo and Gusein-Zade, later stated as conjectures by Leviant--Shustin and by Fomin--Pylyavskyy--Shustin--Thurston. In particular we overcome the main obstruction that remained posed by conjugate pairs of nonreal branches. Our new main ingredient is a construction that produces the divide from a nodal smoothing of two normalization disks. This is what we call the trace map. For real branches, it recovers Gusein-Zade's construction using Chebyshev polynomials. For pairs of complex conjugate branches with distinct tangents, the construction gives an explicit formula for the divide in terms of the Puiseux data. The general method consists in a delicate combination of the trace map with A'Campo's translations and contractions to produce divides and real morsifications for all reduced real plane curve singularities.

entries.name: Weighted bond posets and a new chromatic symmetric function
entries.abstract: The classical bond lattice of a graph was used in a formula of Whitney to compute the chromatic polynomial. In this paper, we use weighted versions of the bond lattice, to introduce and study a new polynomial and a new symmetric function invariant of a graph. Examples of the new polynomial invariant include the classical Narayana polynomials (for the path graph), the tree-Eulerian polynomials (for the complete graph), and the binomial-Eulerian polynomials (for the star graph). These examples suggest an interesting connection to $h$-polynomials of general graph-associahedra. We prove that for any chordal graph, our polynomial graph invariant is $γ$-positive. Multiweighted bond posets yield a symmetric function graph invariant that is an analog of the chromatic polynomial. The highest degree homogeneous component of this symmetric function is of particular interest. The parking function symmetric function introduced by Haiman arises as an example, as do symmetric functions studied by the first author in connection with multibracketed Lie algebras and with colored exterior algebras. The $γ$-positivity result mentioned above is a specialization of an $e$-positivity result for the highest degree homogeneous component, which we prove for any chordal graph using the theory of lexicographic shellability. We conjecture that this symmetric function is Schur-log-concave, which specializes to Huh's log-concavity theorem for the chromatic polynomial.

entries.name: Fröberg's Conjecture for Products of Linear Forms: Split Powers and Inherited Syzygies
entries.abstract: Fröberg's conjecture predicts the Hilbert series of a polynomial ring modulo general forms. We study explicit products of linear forms over fields of characteristic zero. In four variables, six $d$th powers fail to attain the predicted series for $d\ge4$. We fix seven rational directions, take five $d$th powers, and split the sixth generator between the two remaining directions with exponents $\lceil d/2\rceil$ and $\lfloor d/2\rfloor$. The quotient has the predicted series for $1\le d\le30$. For every $\varepsilon>0$ and all sufficiently large $d$, its Hilbert function agrees with the prediction in every degree $q\le(11/5-\varepsilon)d$ or $q\ge(73/32+\varepsilon)d$. In contrast, for $d\ge4$ the predicted series cannot occur if each of the six forms has a linear factor of multiplicity at least $(15d+91)/16$. In three variables, relations among five powers $L_i^e$ give relations among the products $L_i^eM_i$. For five general pairs of linear forms and $e\ge36$, these relations and the pure-power Hilbert function give a lower bound whose error is at most $55$ in every degree and is zero through degree $\lfloor(7e+5)/4\rfloor-2$. The maximum excess over the comparison proposed by Shapiro is $(10/3)e+O(\sqrt e)$.

entries.name: Todd's relation conjecture and binary relations for multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
entries.abstract: We prove Todd's relation conjecture: all $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear relations of Thakur's multiple zeta values are generated from the fundamental binary relation by the operators $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}\circ \mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$; moreover they are also generated by $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$, $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}\circ\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{S}}$. The $\mathcal{B}^{\ast\mathrm{S}}$-part of this conjecture has been proved by Chang, Chen and Mishiba. We prove the whole conjecture for Carlitz multiple polylogarithm values, which implies the $\mathcal{B}^{\mathrm{S}}$-part for multiple zeta values. We also determine all fixed relations and binary relations. Let $\mathfrak{BR}^{\mathrm{S}}_w$ be the $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear space spanned by binary relations of weight $w$, and let $\operatorname{Fix}^{\mathrm{S}}_w$ be the $\mathbb{F}_q(θ)$-linear space spanned by fixed relations. We derive generating functions $\sum_{w\ge 1}\bigl(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}\operatorname{Fix}^{\mathrm{S}}_w\bigr)x^w=\frac{x^{q+1}(1-x)}{(1-2x)(1-2x+x^{q+1})}$ and $\sum_{w\ge 1}\bigl(\dim_{\mathbb{F}_q(θ)}\mathfrak{BR}^{\mathrm{S}}_w\bigr)x^w=\frac{x^q(1-x)}{(1-2x)(1-2x+x^{q+1})}.$ Our results are based on the recent work of Im-Kim-Ngo Dac on the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations of Thakur's multiple zeta values, and a system of transfer theorems between multiple zeta values and multiple polylogarithm values.

entries.name: On the variation of slopes over moduli stacks of Galois representations
entries.abstract: In studying slopes of p-adic eigenforms, focusing on eigenforms with a fixed residual Galois representation is a standard approach. In this paper, we go further and explicitly study how slopes vary as the residual representations vary over a characteristic p space that is closely related to Emerton and Gee's moduli stack of Galois representations. This space, which was introduced in work of Dotto, Emerton, and Gee, is simply a chain of projective lines. We prove that as we move in one direction along this chain the slopes of eigenforms satisfy a snaking property: the n-th slope increases (resp. decreases) for n odd (resp. n even). Our method of proof involves first showing that another sequence of slopes, called the k-derivative slopes, follows its own snaking pattern over the moduli. This is quite interesting in its own right, as these slopes are closely related to slopes of L-invariants attached to eigenforms of level exactly divisible by p. As a consequence, we show that the authors' ghost conjecture, recently proven by Liu, Truong, Xiao, and Zhao, is "stable under direct sums". We determine how p-adic slopes of modular forms vary as their associated Galois representations modulo p vary over moduli of Galois representations. As a consequence, we show that the authors' ghost conjecture recently proven by Liu, Truong, Xiao, and Zhao is "stable under direct sums".

entries.name: A $\sqrt{2}$-Approximation to the Bilu-Linial Conjecture
entries.abstract: Bilu and Linial conjectured that if $d\ge 2$, then every $d$-regular graph $G$ has an edge signing $σ:E(G)\to\{-1,1\}$ such that its signed adjacency matrix $A_σ$ satisfies the Ramanujan bound \begin{equation*} ρ(A_σ)\le 2\sqrt{d-1} \end{equation*} and they proved that \begin{equation*} ρ(A_σ)=O\!\left(\sqrt{d\log^3 d}\right). \end{equation*} Using a method of interlacing polynomials, Marcus, Spielman, and Srivastava confirmed one side of this conjecture that there is a signing $σ$ for which \[ λ_{\max}(A_σ)\le 2\sqrt{d-1}. \] By constructing an auxiliary bipartite graph from a balanced orientation of $G$ and applying a bipartite signing argument, we prove that every finite simple graph $G$ of maximum degree $d\ge 3$ admits an edge signing $σ$ such that \[ ρ(A_σ) \le 4\sqrt{\left\lceil \frac d2\right\rceil-1} \le 2\sqrt{2(d-1)}. \] This gives a new proof of Ravichandran and Srivastava's bound $2\sqrt{2(d-1)}$.

entries.name: There Are No Nontrivial Perfect Codes in the Johnson Scheme
entries.abstract: In his seminal work from 1973, Delsarte conjectured that the Johnson schemes admit no nontrivial perfect codes. We prove this fundamental conjecture which is central in combinatorial coding theory. Our arguments combine lower bounds on the design strength of a perfect code with divisibility conditions for the size of a metric ball. We show that the ball size divides the greatest common divisor of specified binomial coefficients. An exact formula for this gcd implies squarefreeness and localizes a unique power of each prime divisor of the ball size to a short interval. Lloyd polynomials, explicit prime estimates, and bounds for linear forms in logarithms then exclude all radii except for $1$ and $2$. Additional arithmetic arguments handle these two remaining radii.

entries.name: Nearly optimal packings of equally sized rainbow forests
entries.abstract: For every $\varepsilon>0$, we prove that whenever $m$ is sufficiently large in terms of $\varepsilon$ and $1\le k\le2m$, every simple graph with $km$ edges and at most $m$ edges of each color contains at least $(1-\varepsilon)m$ edge-disjoint forests, each with $k$ edges of distinct colors. This gives the packing conjectured by Montgomery, Pokrovskiy, and Sudakov throughout this range, even when adjacent edges may have the same color. For every $k>2m$ there is a graph on $k$ vertices with $km$ edges of distinct colors and no $k$-edge forest. Applied to $K_n$, the theorem gives $(1-o(1))\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ edge-disjoint rainbow spanning trees whenever each color occurs on at most $\lfloor n/2\rfloor$ edges.

entries.name: Agnostic Smoothed Online Regression with Adversarial Responses
entries.abstract: We study smoothed online prediction with bounded adversarial responses. This widely studied framework bridges i.i.d. sampling and adversarial covariate selection through a smoothness parameter $\textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}}$, which bounds conditional covariate densities relative to a fixed, unknown base measure. We propose Hedge-Cover, an information-theoretic algorithm that achieves sublinear regret $\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{\text{Pdim}(\mathcal{F}) \textsf{C}_{\textsf{cov}} T})$ for function classes with bounded pseudo-dimension. The algorithm aggregates a carefully constructed family of experts using Hedge, with a prior that links regret to the number of disagreements between a consistent selector and a target function. We bound this number by exploiting covariate smoothness. This answers an open problem posed in \cite{blanchard2025agnostic} on the minimax optimal adaptive regret of the smoothed online regression problem. We establish a matching lower bound for the class of linear predictors. The main intricacy of the lower bound lies in explicitly constructing a challenging sequential covariate distribution supported on mutually orthogonal hyperplanes.
